goal: Discard exactly the terminal JobAttemptFaulted of the first attempt through a test local typed send pipe, so the product itself has to escalate Running -> CheckingStatus -> Suspect -> JobAttemptFaulted with RetryDelay -> RetryAttempt 1 -> Completed.

whatWorks.injectionFires: The typed filter is invoked for the reported fault and discards it. The fixture reaches the point where the discard is observed.
whatWorks.noProductChange: No product, runtime or public API file was touched at any point of this attempt.

whatDoesNotWork.statement: Discarding the message in the pipe does not prevent its delivery. The attempt saga and the job saga still consume the very JobAttemptFaulted that the filter discarded, the attempt goes to Faulted, its status check is unscheduled, and no status check is ever sent.
whatDoesNotWork.logEvidence: The bus log of the same run shows one SEND of JobAttemptFaulted followed by RECEIVE on /job-attempt and /job with the same message id, then JobFaulted, JobSlotReleased and CancelScheduledMessage.

interceptionPointsTried.point: bus send pipe, ConfigureSend with a typed IFilter<SendContext<JobAttemptFaulted>>
bus publish pipe, ConfigurePublish with a typed IFilter<PublishContext<JobAttemptFaulted>>
typed send topology, Send<JobAttemptFaulted> with an IMessageSendTopology

interceptionPointsTried.result: invoked once and discarded, delivery still happened

openTechnicalQuestion: Exactly one pipe invocation discards the message and the same message is still delivered to both saga endpoints. The delivering path is therefore not one of the four pipes above. The most plausible remaining explanation is that the publish is captured inside the consuming scope and flushed outside the filtered pipe, which would make a send side interception unable to suppress it at all.

correctedEarlierClaims.reason: That conclusion came from a confounded observation channel. Console output of the fixture is not captured in the console stream of the test run and not in the TRX either. Only counters reported inside the test failure message are a valid channel here, and they show the publish filter is invoked.
